bounded_contexts.name: workflow-runtime
bounded_contexts.description: Workflow execution substrate spanning spec-store, execution-engine, state-machine, event-bus, replay-debugger, trigger-orchestrator, plugin substrate, and cross-cell/audit bridges. Preview foundation now includes source-level execution-engine kernel and domain layers with run/step/retry/SLA-timer entities, protocol-neutral store/dispatcher/retry/timer/ephemeral-state port traits, policy/spec/replay/scheduler evidence binding, scope validation, dispatch/retry/timer planning, a source-level execution-engine usecase that validates request/idempotency/trace metadata, preserves deterministic idempotent replay/conflict semantics, loads runs through abstract store ports, delegates to the domain, updates run/step state, invokes abstract dispatcher/retry-policy/timer ports, maps store/dispatch/timer/retry failures to redaction-safe metadata-only receipts, a source-level in-memory execution adapter bundle that implements abstract run-store, step-dispatcher, retry-policy, and SLA-timer ports with tenant-scoped maps, optimistic version conflicts, injected-epoch timer firing, deterministic retry delays, metadata-only action recording, a plan-only Postgres execution adapter defining tenant-scoped run/step/timer DDL, ON CONFLICT run/step/timer upsert plans, expected-version status updates, dispatcher outbox enqueue plans, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED timer scan plans, redaction-safe row mapping, affected-row conflict mapping, and unsafe metadata denial, a pure state-machine kernel for AsyncAPI lifecycle events, a policy-bound domain layer that attaches tenant/spec/policy/replay evidence before kernel delegation, a source-level usecase that loads current checkpoints and appends accepted checkpoints through a sealed store port with optimistic expected-sequence metadata, a framework-free API boundary that validates version/tenant/principal/authorization metadata, maps API event bodies to typed lifecycle events, preserves idempotent response replay, and projects checkpoints into OpenAPI/proto status DTOs, an in-memory preview adapter that implements the checkpoint-store port with tenant-scoped monotonic append/load semantics for source-level integration tests, plus a plan-only Postgres checkpoint adapter defining tenant-scoped current-load SQL, optimistic append SQL, unique-key DDL, row mapping, and affected-row conflict mapping without executing database I/O while preserving deterministic checkpoint sequencing, tenant/spec invariants, pause/resume/cancel guards, replay-safe transition denials, and no concrete storage, network, HTTP serving, signing, or runtime side effects. It now includes a source-level REST route facade over the execution-engine API boundary for start/dispatch/retry/timer command routes. It now includes a source-level worker seam for leased job validation, usecase orchestration, retry classification, and cold-start resume throttling. It now includes a source-level SDK facade that builds typed start/dispatch/retry/timer command plans over the REST/API boundary, preserves caller-supplied idempotency/version/authorization metadata, forbids automatic retries by default, and supports in-process preview execution without HTTP client or cloud side effects. It now includes a source-level app composition root over the SDK, REST/API, worker, and in-memory adapter seams; validates Oyatie Cloud dogfood tenant-workload metadata refs before composition; exposes startup/liveness/readiness probe decisions with drain-aware readiness; emits OpenTelemetry-shaped service identity attributes; and supports in-process preview start/dispatch/timer execution without runtime binary, Kubernetes, cloud, or tenant-scheduling side effects. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator kernel that admits cron, webhook, event-bus, manual, API, workflow-spawn, and ontology triggers through policy-bound metadata, HMAC/nonce refs, CloudEvents-shaped envelope refs, schedule due/catchup/pause/overlap decisions, replay suppression, and raw content/secret rejection without scheduler runtime, webhook server, event-bus consumer, run-start side effects, cloud deployment, or tenant scheduling. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator domain layer that binds trigger admission to tenant, principal, Cedar-shaped policy decision/evidence/bundle refs, source-surface evidence, scheduler/webhook/event contract refs, replay epoch, audit-chain, trace, correlation, and idempotency scope before kernel delegation; maps accepted, deferred, denied, and replay-suppressed kernel outcomes into domain/audit refs; rejects scope/source drift and raw content/secret metadata without echo; and performs no Cedar evaluation, scheduler execution, HMAC verification, HTTP serving, event-bus consumption, run creation, durable trigger storage, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator usecase that validates request, idempotency, and trace refs before domain delegation, applies deterministic in-memory idempotent replay/conflict semantics, maps accepted/deferred/denied/replay-suppressed domain outcomes into metadata-only receipts and audit events, preserves sorted evidence/non-claim refs, redacts raw content/secret metadata, and performs no concrete idempotency store, trigger registry store, policy engine, Cedar evaluation, scheduler runtime, webhook server, HMAC verification, event-bus consumer, run creation, durable trigger storage, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator API boundary that validates method, route, contract version, tenant, principal, authorization, idempotency, source/kind pairing, and safe metadata before mapping API DTOs into the trigger-orchestrator usecase; preserves in-memory API idempotent replay/conflict semantics; maps accepted/deferred/suppressed receipts to stable 202 DTOs and denied/invalid/conflicting requests to RFC 9457-shaped problem details; rejects raw content/secret metadata without echo; and performs no HTTP serving, serialization-framework work, concrete storage, scheduler execution, webhook serving, HMAC verification, event-bus consumption, run creation, durable idempotency storage, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator REST boundary that maps HTTP-shaped method/path requests to the trigger-orchestrator API, rejects route/method/body route drift before delegation, returns application/json success DTOs and application/problem+json problem DTOs, preserves API idempotent replay/conflict behavior through the in-process API, redacts raw content/secret metadata, and performs no HTTP serving, socket binding, serialization-framework work, concrete storage, scheduler execution, webhook serving, HMAC verification, event-bus consumption, run creation, durable idempotency storage, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator worker seam that validates leased trigger job metadata, honors not-before and lease-expiry gates before API delegation, invokes the in-process trigger-orchestrator API, maps accepted/deferred/suppressed/denied outcomes into metadata-only worker receipts and audit-shaped events, preserves API idempotent replay/conflict behavior, models capped deterministic retry scheduling for retryable API unavailability, plans cold-start resume throttling, redacts raw content/secret metadata, and performs no durable queue polling, Valkey lease I/O, scheduler execution, webhook serving, HMAC verification, event-bus consumption, run creation, network I/O, filesystem access, wall-clock reads, random/UUID generation, Kubernetes calls, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator SDK facade that builds typed scheduler, Studio webhook, sibling event-bus, manual UI, API command, workflow-spawn, and ontology-projection trigger evaluation plans; binds version, tenant, principal, authorization, trace, idempotency, route, and source-specific metadata; disables automatic retries by default; supports in-process preview execution through the REST/API boundary; redacts raw content/secret metadata; and performs no HTTP client work, DNS, sockets, serialization-framework work, credential loading, random/UUID generation, wall-clock reads, automatic retries, durable idempotency, queueing, signing, filesystem access, Kubernetes calls, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling. It now includes a source-level trigger-orchestrator app composition root over the SDK, REST/API, and worker seams; validates Oyatie Cloud dogfood tenant-workload metadata refs before composition; exposes startup/liveness/readiness probe decisions with drain-aware readiness; emits OpenTelemetry-shaped service identity attributes; delegates in-process preview trigger evaluation and worker resume planning; redacts raw prompt/output/payload/secret metadata; and performs no runtime binary, scheduler/webhook/event-bus execution, run-creation, Kubernetes, cloud, or tenant-scheduling side effects. It now includes a source-level event-bus kernel that models CloudEvents-shaped workflow event envelopes, AsyncAPI-shaped channel/message refs, tenant/cell/residency binding, deterministic idempotent delivery keys, subscription delivery decisions, safe evidence refs, and raw prompt/output/payload/secret rejection without broker connections, topic creation, network I/O, serialization-framework work, durable outbox/inbox writes, consumer group coordination, offset commits, payload materialization, Kubernetes, cloud, or tenant-scheduling side effects. It now includes a source-level event-bus domain layer that binds publish and delivery intents to tenant, cell, principal, policy decision/evidence/bundle, residency, trace, and audit refs before kernel delegation; authorizes event-kind/channel allowlists; maps publish and delivery outcomes into redaction-safe receipts; rejects policy drift and raw prompt/output/payload/secret metadata without echo; and performs no policy-engine execution, broker connections, durable outbox/inbox writes, consumer group coordination, offset commits, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling side effects. It now includes a source-level event-bus usecase that validates request, idempotency, trace, policy/residency binding, publish intent, subscription intent, and delivery candidate metadata before domain delegation; applies deterministic in-memory idempotent replay/conflict semantics for publish and delivery commands; maps accepted, denied, and domain-denied outcomes into metadata-only receipts and audit events; rejects raw prompt/output/payload/secret-shaped refs without echo; and performs no concrete idempotency store, broker connection, topic creation, network I/O, serialization-framework work, durable outbox/inbox writes, consumer group coordination, offset commits, payload materialization, signing, filesystem access, random/UUID generation, wall-clock reads, Kubernetes calls, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling side effects. It now includes a source-level event-bus API boundary that validates method, route, contract version, tenant, principal, authorization, idempotency, policy/residency/audit refs, CloudEvents-shaped event metadata, AsyncAPI-shaped channel metadata, publish bodies, and delivery-evaluation bodies before usecase delegation; preserves in-memory API idempotent replay/conflict semantics; maps accepted publish, accepted delivery, delivery-denied, invalid, domain-denied, and conflicting outcomes into OpenAPI/RFC-9457-shaped success/problem DTOs; rejects raw prompt/output/payload/secret-shaped refs without echo; and performs no HTTP serving, serialization-framework work, concrete storage, broker connection, topic creation, network I/O, durable idempotency storage, durable outbox/inbox writes, consumer group coordination, offset commits, signing, Kubernetes calls, cloud deployment, or tenant workload scheduling side effects. It now includes a source-level event-bus app composition root over the SDK, REST/API, and worker seams; validates Oyatie Cloud dogfood tenant-workload metadata refs before composition; exposes startup/liveness/readiness probe decisions with drain-aware readiness; emits OpenTelemetry-shaped service and Kubernetes namespace attributes; delegates in-process preview publish/delivery evaluation and worker resume planning; redacts raw prompt/output/payload/secret metadata; and performs no runtime binary, broker/topic/consumer-group/offset execution, Kubernetes, cloud, or tenant-scheduling side effects.

naming_justifications: workflow-engine is a BNF v4.1 kebab-case microservice slug; generated names follow oya-workflow-engine-<bounded-context>-<layer>, with layer rest from ADR-0105's 13-layer enum.

capacity_model.notes: Durable execution and tenant-authored workflow/plugin steps scale by active workflow run, not by editor users or request fan-out.

pod_runtime_tier_justification: Workflow Engine is the tenant workflow execution substrate and includes tenant-authored workflow/custom-node execution surfaces, so ADR-0338 requires Tier 0 isolation rather than the first-party app default.
